afonso.summary: Mozambican IT professional and innovation self-taught with over 6 years of experience. Graduated in Multimedia, lead RPA Mozambique and specialist in AI and scalable digital solutions.
afonso.bio:
Afonso Domingos is a Mozambican IT professional and innovation self-taught with over 6 years of experience. Graduated in Multimedia, lead RPA Mozambique and specialist in AI and scalable digital solutions.

Throughout his journey, Afonso has stood out in creating technological ecosystems that solve real problems. As founder of Inscreva-se, he brought a vision of simplification and efficiency to the African event market, integrating artificial intelligence and automated processes to maximize results.

His specialties include software development, robotic process automation (RPA), product strategy and technical team leadership. He believes technology should be a facilitator of human progress and works tirelessly to democratize access to cutting-edge solutions.

culpa.role: Co-Founder - Inscreva-se | President of ODEI and CCA | Vice Director of the African Union Youth Commission (Southern Africa)
culpa.summary: Young leader, consultant, and specialist in Education, Technology, Science, and Innovation, former Commissioner of the African Union Youth Union. Currently Vice Director of the Youth Commission of the UA for Southern Africa and founder of CCA and ODEI.
culpa.bio:
Culpa Francisco Xavier is a young leader, consultant, and specialist in Education, Technology, Science, and Innovation, former Commissioner of the African Union Youth Union. Currently Vice Director of the African Union Youth Commission for Southern Africa. He is the founder of CCA – Consulting and Coaching Agency and ODEI – Organization for Child Development and Education.

With over 18 years of experience in projects related to early childhood, youth, leadership, and social transformation, he has been recognized as a Young Person of Change by Save the Children and a Reference Student by Eduardo Mondlane University, in addition to having Trainer training from UNICEF.
